title: Tranche inventory mapping: $/1M tokens by instance class
content:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet converts regional GPU inventory (by instance class) into tranche sizes tied to an operational $/1M tokens metric. The goal is to provide a fast lookup for product/finance/infra to translate a target token budget into how many GPU-hours (and nodes) we should reserve at different confidence levels.

High level approach (short):
1) Map instance class -> on-peak GPU-hour price by region (market prices + negotiated reserved uplift).
2) Convert model throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) into tokens per GPU-hour for typical workloads (weighted seq-length and response ratio).
3) Compute baseline $/1M tokens = (GPU-hour price) / (tokens per GPU-hour) * 1e6.
4) Apply overhead multipliers for small-batch penalty, KV memory pressure, and observed tail latency inefficiency.
5) Produce tranche table: safety-stock (%) and recommended commit (GPU-hours / month) by region & SLA tier.

Assumptions (configurable cells):
- Model family mix (prod): 60% chat-extended (avg seq 800 tokens), 30% completion-medium (avg seq 200), 10% embeddings/batch small.
- Base throughput estimates (tokens/sec per A100-80GB equivalent):
  * chat-extended: 18k tok/s (kv heavy, slows after 1k context)
  * completion-medium: 52k tok/s
  * embeddings-batch: 120k tok/s (amortized microbatches)
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour = tokens/sec * 3600 * efficiency_factor (range 0.6-0.9 depending on batching). Default efficiency_factor = 0.78.
- Small-batch penalty multiplier = 1.20 for <32 concurrent slots.
- KV-cache hit improvement factor = 1.15 when 30% prefix reuse.
- GPU-hour pricing (example snapshot):
  Region     | instance-class | spot $/GPU-hr | reserved $/GPU-hr (monthly committed)
  us-west1    A100-80GB        2.10           3.60
  us-east1    A100-80GB        1.95           3.30
  eu-west1    A100-80GB        2.25           3.85
  ap-southeast1 A100-80GB      2.85           4.40

Sample calculation (us-west1, reserved):
- Pick baseline throughput: blended tokens/sec per GPU = 0.6*18k + 0.3*52k + 0.1*120k = 10.8k + 15.6k + 12k = 38.4k tok/s
- tokens per GPU-hour (raw) = 38,400 * 3600 = 138,240,000 tok/hr
- efficiency_factor = 0.78 => effective = 107,827,200 tok/hr
- reserved price = $3.60 / GPU-hr => $/1M tokens = 3.60 / 107.8272 * 1e6 = $33.38 per 1M tokens
- Apply small-batch penalty (assume current slot count small) => multiply by 1.20 => $40.06 per 1M tokens
- Apply KV cache benefit if applicable (e.g., 30% prefix reuse reduces compute) => divide by 1.15 => $34.83 per 1M tokens
  Note: order of multipliers matters; we present them as scenario modifiers rather than absolute transforms.

Regional quick-reference table (blended model mix, efficiency 0.78, reserved pricing):
Region | reserved $/GPU-hr | eff tok/hr | base $/1M | small-batch adj | kv-cache adj | scenario $/1M (both)
us-west1 | 3.60 | 107,827,200 | 33.38 | 40.06 | 34.83 | 40.06* (if no kv-cache)
us-east1 | 3.30 | 107,827,200 | 30.61 | 36.73 | 31.89 | 36.73
eu-west1 | 3.85 | 107,827,200 | 35.69 | 42.83 | 37.52 | 42.83
ap-southeast1 | 4.40 | 107,827,200 | 40.79 | 48.95 | 42.57 | 48.95

Tranche sizing rules (recommended):
- Tranche = base_commit + safety_stock. base_commit = expected monthly GPU-hr consumption (derived from target tokens/month / eff tok/hr * 1hr).
- Safety stock tiers: conservative (30%), standard (15%), aggressive (5%). Use conservative for critical SLAs and standard for high-usage self-serve customers.
- Commit rounding: round to nearest node (N GPUs per node). We have mixed node sizes: 8x A100-80GB (default), 4x A100-80GB (dense). Round up.

Worked example: customer target = 500M tokens / month, region us-east1, reserved pricing.
- required GPU-hours (raw) = 500M / 107.8272M = 4.637 GPU-hrs -> monthly multiply: actually this is hours; check: 107.8272M tok per GPU-hour -> so 500M / 107.8272M = 4.637 GPU-hours total (that's small because tokens per GPU-hour huge) -> this is per-hour estimate; for month you multiply by 1? Need clarity: we mean 500M tokens per month -> GPU-hrs needed = 500M / eff tok/hr = 4.637 GPU-hours (total per month). That's quite small; note: confirm unit sanity.
- That's unrealistic for prod; more realistic customer at scale: 50B tokens/month => 50,000M / 107.8272M = 463.7 GPU-hrs/month -> base_commit = 464 GPU-hrs -> safety stock standard 15% => 533 GPU-hrs -> with 8x nodes = 533 / (24*30*8) nodes? Wait: converting commit to nodes requires commit term.
- For monthly reserved capacity we express commit in GPU-hours/month and then map to node count assuming 720 hours/month per GPU: nodes_needed = ceil(GPU-hrs/month / (GPUs_per_node * 720)). Example: 533 GPU-hrs/month / (8*720) = 533 / 5760 = 0.093 nodes -> round up to 1 node (minimum). This highlights low absolute GPU-hours for token-only workloads; most high-consumption workloads are concurrent, not just monthly aggregate. Use concurrent slot modelling for production.

Concurrent-slot modelling (recommended for capacity correctness):
- Convert tokens/sec demand to concurrent GPUs required: concurrent_gpus = peak_tokens_per_sec / eff_tokens_per_second_per_gpu.
- Peak_tokens_per_sec derived from QPS * avg tokens per response. For example, 200 qps * 200 tokens = 40k tok/sec -> concurrent_gpus = 40k / 38.4k = 1.04 GPUs -> round up to 2 GPUs.
- Map concurrency to monthly GPU-hrs: monthly_gpu_hrs = concurrent_gpus * 24 * 30 (720h). Add utilization factor (expected busy fraction), e.g., 0.65.
- This method yields realistic committed GPU-hour numbers for reserved planning.

Example using concurrency: target steady qps=150, avg_response=350 tok => peak_tok/s = 52,500 tok/s -> concurrent_gpus = 52,500 / 38,400 = 1.37 -> round up to 2 GPUs -> monthly_gpu_hrs_nominal = 2 * 720 = 1,440 GPU-hrs -> utilization factor 0.65 -> expected burn 936 GPU-hrs/month -> with 15% safety = 1,076 GPU-hrs/month -> nodes needed (8-GPU nodes) = ceil(1,076 / (8*720)) = ceil(1,076 / 5,760) = 1 node (again low due to large monthly hours per node). For higher throughput clusters this scales.

Tail-risk and burst buffer sizing:
- Reserve an additional burst buffer layer in cheaper regions or use spot capacity. We recommend a burst tranche sized at either X% of base_commit or N GPU-hours (whichever is larger). Suggested defaults: 30% of base_commit or 400 GPU-hrs, capped at 3 nodes.
- Spot savings vs preemptions: model expected effective $/1M by applying preemption factor (e.g., 0.75 price * 1.12 re-run overhead multiplier).

Operational checklist (actionable cells to add to sheet):
- Inputs to expose on top row: target tokens/month, peak QPS, avg tokens/resp, region, desired SLA tier, batching efficiency (0.5-0.95), KV reuse fraction.
- Outputs: GPU-hrs/month (raw), GPU-hrs/month (with util), nodes to reserve, $/1M tokens baseline, adjusted $/1M tokens (small-batch, KV, spot), recommended tranche (base + safety + burst).
- Quick sensitivity toggles: +/−10% price, +/−10% throughput, alternate model mix presets (chat-heavy, completion-heavy, embeddings-heavy).

Open questions / next steps:
- Validate throughput numbers against daily perf harness (Jing to run mixed-workload perf test on staging A100-equivalent).
- Confirm node consolidation policy (min node commit per region) — affects rounding and small customers.
- Tie to billing: make an automated pipeline to pull committed reserved price and spot price daily and refresh $/1M cells.

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet intentionally mixes aggregate-month and concurrency-first views. For long-term commits we should prefer the concurrency->monthly conversion to avoid under-committing.
- The big risk for teams using tokens-only metrics is unit mismatch: tokens per GPU-hour is large so small token volumes look trivial but concurrency drives committed capacity.

Raw table for copy-paste into sheet (columns comma-separated):
region,instance_class,reserved_$per_gpu_hr,spot_$per_gpu_hr,eff_tok_per_hr,base_$per_1M,small_batch_adj,kv_cache_adj,concurrency_scenario_notes
us-west1,A100-80GB,3.60,2.10,107827200,33.38,40.06,34.83,"blended mix, eff 0.78"
us-east1,A100-80GB,3.30,1.95,107827200,30.61,36.73,31.89,"blended mix, eff 0.78"
eu-west1,A100-80GB,3.85,2.25,107827200,35.69,42.83,37.52,"blended mix, eff 0.78"
ap-southeast1,A100-80GB,4.40,2.85,107827200,40.79,48.95,42.57,"blended mix, eff 0.78"

Please review numbers (especially throughput) and push any measured perf data into the perf sheet reference: CONFLUENCE-4201. If we agree, I will convert to a canonical Google Sheet with formula cells and sensitivity toggles and add per-customer tabs for quick commits.

-- Aisha
